questions.stem: What is the main difference between a scheduled trigger and a file arrival trigger?

options.text: File arrival runs only once a day
A schedule needs Unity Catalog; file arrival does not
A schedule runs at set times whether or not there is new data; file arrival runs when data lands

questions.explanation: Time-based triggers follow the clock; data-driven triggers follow new data.

questions.stem: A source system publishes its daily table at an unpredictable hour. Which trigger reduces wasted and late runs?
questions.explanation: A table update trigger runs the job when the table is updated, rather than at a fixed time.

questions.stem: Finance needs a report at exactly 07:00 for a meeting, even when no data changed overnight. Which trigger fits best?
questions.explanation: When the business needs a fixed time, a time-based schedule is the right trigger.

questions.stem: Which statements about data-driven triggers are true? Choose two.

options.text: They avoid runs that find nothing new to process
They start runs in response to new files or table updates
They guarantee the job runs at a fixed time each day
They work on any local disk path

questions.explanation: File arrival and table update triggers react to data, which avoids empty runs, but do not keep a clock.

questions.stem: A team schedules a job every 5 minutes to check for new files, and most runs find none. What change fits better?

options.text: Switch to a file arrival trigger

questions.explanation: A file arrival trigger replaces polling on a schedule and only runs when files land.
